fields.why: The text states significant differences across race/ethnicity groups and education levels, and Tables 1–2 show five age groups.
Race/ethnicity, education (SES, 3 levels) and age (5 levels) are the SPDs with 3+ groups; sex, insurance and disability are two-level here.

A blanket 'Wald chi square tests ... within-group differences' under specific group-vs-group claims fits per-group vs referent only (brief's t-test example); 'Only significant differences are reported' could support pairwise (all pairs) for race, or the tests could be per-characteristic omnibus. Age has no reported difference, so side by side is defensible despite the flag; race n_groups is arguably 5 (Other not compared), not 6.

brief_issues: The brief does not say whether 'only significant differences are reported' counts like the QuickStats 'all other differences were not significant' line for pairwise (all pairs), nor how to read a characteristic with no reported difference when a blanket test method is stated.
